findings.issue: If the credit lookup gets a 404 (payment-service is older than PR-B) and the order already has a payment row, prepareRefund skips the legacy check and the refund goes ahead. This can pay twice. The case is a COD return that is still PICKED_UP and has a pre-F-09 return-rest-<id> credit made after a non-503 refund error, for example a 409 on a COD_PENDING row. If order-service PR-B is deployed before payment-service PR-B, that return gets a second refund. So condition 5 (the check runs on every attempt, even when the row exists) holds only if the deploy order is followed. The same applies if the lookup returns 200 with an empty body: credit is null and the refund goes ahead. The CTO decision accepts the 404 behaviour ('proceeds as today'), and it is no worse than today's F-09 code, so I rate this minor.
findings.fix: Either answer 503 whenever the lookup fails or returns a null body, with or without a row, since this only matters during the deploy window and payment-service deploys first. Or make 'payment-service before order-service' a hard gate in pr.md and the release checklist, and change design.md, which says 'either order is safe'.

findings.issue: When legacyPaid is true, the wallet leg still sends the frozen wallet amount under return-wallet-<id>. The pre-F-09 code credited a pro-rata walletShare under the same key. The key dedupes, so nothing is paid twice. But only the rest amount is checked against the legacy credit. If today's frozen wallet leg differs from the legacy wallet credit, the key dedupe silently keeps the old amount. The return is then marked REFUNDED with a wallet leg that does not match its frozen figure, and nothing reports it.
findings.fix: In the legacy branch, also look up return-wallet-<id>. When it exists and its amount differs from plan.wallet() by compareTo, treat it as COD LEGACY CREDIT MISMATCH (409 with an ERROR, no money moved), or at least log an ERROR.

summary: I found no blocker or major issue in PR-B. Legacy-credit settle rule: it runs only on route PAYMENT_WALLET for COD orders (spec.cod()). WALLET-method orders route to DIRECT_WALLET and card orders do no lookup. It runs on every attempt while the rest leg is not SUCCEEDED, before the wallet leg and before any ensure or refund call. It matches user by equals, amount by compareTo and currency by equals. A null currency or a mismatch gives a 409 with an ERROR log naming only the return and order ids, and no money moves. The four C6 tests and mutant M1 confirm this. An exact match marks the rest leg SUCCEEDED, makes no refund call, and later retries skip the lookup. findCredit filters type='CREDIT' on a UNIQUE idempotency_key, so .optional() cannot be ambiguous. Refund cap: unchanged in freezeLegs (mutant M2). A legacy-settled rest leg counts as a SUCCEEDED sibling, the ensured row amount is total minus wallet, and payment-service still caps refunds at the row amount. Cancelled or undelivered orders: ensure checks cancelled before EXISTING. collect and prepareRefund call codCollectedNow only for CREATED or EXISTING rows when deliveredAt is set and the payment status is collected. That status is set in the same save as delivery, and COD_PENDING routes to NONE (mutant M3). New GET /internal/wallet/credits/{key}: InternalTokenFilter guards it. tokenRequired covers no token, a wrong token and an empty token, with a positive control (mutant M4). The gateway has no /internal route, and the existing internalPathsAreNotRouted test covers /internal/**. payment-service has no springdoc, so the endpoint is not in any public OpenAPI. It always answers 200 with only found, userId, amount and currency, and logs nothing. The key is bound as a SQL parameter, so there is no injection. The only caller builds it as 'return-rest-'+UUID. PR-A minors: (1) PaymentFeignClient now also uses NoUserTokenFeignConfig, and a header test with a positive control checks that X-Internal-Token is sent and Authorization is not. (2) The runbook says ERROR. (3) The slow-placement note is added. (4) A COD create over a non-COD row returns at once with no Razorpay wait, and a test checks that razorpay.enabled() is never called. All four are resolved. No new dependency. The re-arm runbook SQL touches only DEAD COD_COLLECTED rows, at most 500 per statement. Two minors remain: the lookup-404-with-row path depends on deploy order, and a legacy wallet-leg amount mismatch is not reported.
